correctness.rationale: For discrete X, Sh(X) is Set^X and ultrafilters select a summand pointwise. At each nonisolated x in a zero-dimensional Hausdorff X, the clopen-neighbourhood tail ultrafilter yields intersection exactly {x} for every large coordinate set. The global tuple of clopen characteristic sections has at x a germ not equal to either constant binary germ, because equality in the filtered colimit of product-sheaf stalks forces a single common neighbourhood W in every selected coordinate; W subset {x} contradicts nonisolation. All quantifiers and categorical operations were checked.

value.rationale: The intrinsic all-zero-dimensional-Hausdorff iff separates infinite discrete spaces from every nondiscrete instance, with no compactness, cardinality or countability assumptions. A fixed binary constant-sheaf input gives an explicit local obstruction at each nonisolated point. This is a natural full classification for the condition needed in the positive enriched Los theorem, though the already known Stone-space obstruction is not counted as new.
